text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT P1 — GPU paging detected in prod-runtime (us-west1). Trigger: page_fault_rate > 200/s. Pager: @eva. Notifying on-call and customer-ops.

eva: I'm on pager. moving to this thread, grabbing recent traces/logs. What's current customer impact?

ben: Quick summary from telemetry: 5-10% 5xx on /v1/generate for `redwood-3b-quant` in us-west1. Prom shows page_faults spike and KV-chain evictions climbing. Sharing short stats now.

ben: prom query highlights: `increase(runtime_gpu_page_faults[1m])` peaked ~320/s at 23:12Z. avg gpu_mem_used ~23.8 GiB / 24 GiB for impacted hosts. `kv_chain_evictions_total` +3.2x during window.

ben: logs snippet:
```
[23:12:18] runtime: page_faults=342 per min, gpu_mem_used=23820MB, total=24576MB
[23:12:20] kv_chain: shard=12 evict=1250 -> 4023 (3.2x)
[23:12:21] allocator: free_regions=12 -> 3, largest_free_region=48MB
```

mohit: Hypothesis: allocator/tensor fragmentation — lots of small free regions, can't satisfy contiguous allocation for KV/cache pages -> pagewalks and heavy GPU paging. Also saw a traffic pattern where some clients briefly spiked batch_size from 4->8 which increases peak working set.

danny: Immediate mitigation I can try: roll routing change to cap batch_size for `redwood-3b-quant` in us-west1 from 8 -> 4 and restart a small canary pool. Will push a canary now.

eva: Do it. Flag mitigation and notify customer-ops for updates.

danny: Pushed canary rollout to 3 hosts. Patch diff: `batch_size: 8 -> 4` on us-west1 route. API call used:
```
curl -s -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/route/update -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-3b-quant","region":"us-west1","batch_size":4}'
# response: 200 OK
```

ben: Canary results: page_fault_rate down to ~90/s on canary hosts, request errors dropped to ~1.2% on those nodes. Latency p50 improved ~150ms. KV evictions on canary returned to baseline. Non-canary hosts still noisy.

customer-ops: Customer impact note: three enterprise customers reported transient 5xx between 23:10-23:25Z; we updated status page and SC already called one of them. No data loss reported.

mohit: Next steps for RCA: collect full nvml/nvprof maps, jemalloc stats, and KV-chain allocator dumps from impacted hosts. Plan a targeted defrag (mem compaction) on a small subset overnight and a controlled rolling restart to reduce fragmentation. Also add detection metric: `free_region_count` and `largest_free_region_bytes` to alert before pagewalk spikes.

eva: Handing follow-up to ben for post-incident RCA. Ben — you're on for the next 8h to own artifacts + draft timeline. Tagging eng-runtime for kernel/allocator review.

ben: Ack. I'll gather traces (nvml + core memory maps), attach `nvidia-smi` dumps and jemalloc snapshots, and write a timeline + hypothesis list. Initial hypothesis: fragmentation + bursty batch-size spikes => unsatisfiable contiguous allocations for KV/cache => heavy GPU pagewalks => service errors. Mitigations: throttle batch spikes, add early fragmentation detection, implement graceful KV-backpressure config.

srebot: Follow-ups created: INC-20260316-342 (collect nvml traces), INC-20260316-343 (schedule defrag job on subset), INC-20260316-344 (customer follow-up / status update).

eva: Closing live coordination thread here. Moving all artifacts to /incidents/2026-03-16-gpu-paging for RCA write-up. Thanks everyone for quick mitigation.

ben: Final note: for immediate protection I'll add a transient rule to limit `batch_size` per-route on surge to avoid repeated spikes until allocator-level fixes land.
